text:
maria: heads-up, running into a deterministic ESM/CJS interop problem when bundling the js sdk for edge runtimes with multiple bundlers (vite/webpack/rollup). minimal repro below, anyone seen this?

maria: repro steps (very short):
1) simple package.json (note: "type": "module") and sdk published with both cjs + esm builds.
2) import in app as `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` and call `Redwood.createClient(...)`
3) build with vite/rollup/webpack, deploy to edge, runtime throws: `TypeError: Redwood.createClient is not a function` or `Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "createClient")`.

maria: package.json snippet:
```json
{
  "name": "example-app",
  "type": "module",
  "dependencies": {
    "redwood-sdk": "^1.2.3"
  }
}
```

maria: dist layout of the SDK (published):
- dist/esm/index.js  (ESM, `export default` + named exports)
- dist/cjs/index.js  (CJS, `module.exports = ...`)
- package.json has `main: "dist/cjs/index.js"`, `module: "dist/esm/index.js"`, and an `exports` map.

ajay: what node + vite/webpack versions? also do you have `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` in tsconfig?

maria: node 18.16, vite 5.0, webpack 5.86, rollup 3.x. tsconfig has `esModuleInterop: false`, `allowSyntheticDefaultImports: false` (default user setup).

sam: hmm, common pattern: bundler picks the cjs entry for some build paths and then `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` becomes `{ default: { createClient: [Function] } }` or the reverse depending on interop. that yields `createClient` undefined at runtime.

louis: can you paste the exact runtime stack? sometimes the shim in edge runtime (esbuild-based) changes how `default` is handled.

maria: CI log excerpt (from failing canary build):
```
Error: Uncaught TypeError: Cannot read properties of undefined (reading "createClient")
  at file:///.netlify/functions/edge-handler.js:42:18
  at async file:///.netlify/functions/edge-handler.js:88:5
```

ci-bot: Build step `yarn build:edge` failed on main/canary (see pipeline 4123). Reaction :face_with_raised_eyebrow:.

ajay: easy-to-miss: rollup/webpack may be consuming `exports` map differently. if package.json has conditional exports and a nested `require` path, some bundlers fall back to cjs. also typescript imports without synthetic default means `import Redwood from '...'` is not guaranteed to map to default. try `import * as Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'` or `const Redwood = require('redwood-sdk')` to see which variant works.

maria: tried `import * as Redwood` — that actually surfaces `createClient` under `Redwood.default.createClient` in vite build, but in webpack it was `Redwood.createClient`. inconsistent across bundlers.

sam: recommended repro: create a very small repo with `type: module`, a ts file: `import Redwood from 'redwood-sdk'; Redwood.createClient(...)` then build with each bundler using conservative config (no special commonjs plugin). if you can share that, we can run locally.

louis: other workaround: publish an explicit ESM-only entry and force consumers to import from `redwood-sdk/esm` or set `exports` with an explicit `import` condition. e.g. package.json exports: { "./package.json": { "default": "./package.json" }, "./*": { "import": "./dist/esm/*.js", "require": "./dist/cjs/*.js" } } — but that can be tricky for tools that don't fully honor `exports`.

ajay: for vite specifically, try `optimizeDeps.exclude: ['redwood-sdk']` or explicitly point `resolve.alias: { 'redwood-sdk': path.resolve(__dirname, 'node_modules/redwood-sdk/dist/esm/index.js') }` as a quick test. that forces ESM.

maria: pasted minimal repro link: https://github.com/redwood/repro-sdk-bundler-edge-interop (private, internal) — contains 3 folders: repro-vite, repro-webpack, repro-rollup. each has the same source file. build + run illustrates mismatch.

sam: also post your SDK's `package.json` published `exports` map and the top of dist files (`dist/esm/index.js`) — sometimes tools transform `export default` into `exports.default =` which then when consumed as CJS becomes nested.

maria: sdk package.json exports map: 
```json
{
  "import": "./dist/esm/index.js",
  "require": "./dist/cjs/index.js"
}
```

maria: dist/esm/index.js head:
```js
export default {
  createClient: (opts) => { /* ... */ }
}
export const createClient = (opts) => defaultExport.createClient(opts)
```

sam: that pattern (default object + named re-export) is suspicious. double-wrapping `createClient` can confuse tree-shaking and interop. try exporting named functions only (no default) and provide a small default that references them if you really want default.

louis: for types: TS consumers with `esModuleInterop: true` won't see issues; consumers without it are more likely to use `import * as Redwood` which interacts differently. consider publishing proper .d.ts that uses `export =` or `export default` patterns consistent with runtime.

maria: thanks — i'll open an SDK issue with the minimal repro and attach CI logs + steps. will try forcing named exports only in a test branch.

ajay: if you want, i can run the three repro folders locally and try the alias/optimizeDeps suggestion.

maria: please do, that'd help. i'll ping once i've pushed test branch.

ci-bot: created ticket: CI-4123 (internal) referencing repro — assigned to @maria.

maria: noted. will follow up with concrete PR that removes default wrapper and adds explicit `exports` import condition. thanks all :thumbsup:
